newsitem.title: USA: Butler MFG to sell unit, sees $2/shr gain.
newsitem.headline: Butler MFG to sell unit, sees $2/shr gain.

text.p: Butler Manufacturing Co said Monday it has agreed to sell its Grain Systems division to CTB Inc for about $33 million in cash.
If the transaction occurs as planned, Butler will realize an after-tax gain of about $15 million or $2.00 per share. Net cash proceeds to Butler will be about $23 million.
Closing is expected to occur within 30 days, according to the preliminary agreement.
CTB is a privately owned company that owns several agricultural equipment entities, including Brock Manufacturing, a grain storage business based in Indiana.

Robert West, chairman and chief executive officer of Butler, said: "The combining of Butler's Grain Systems division with CTB will result in a larger, stronger, geographically diversified company serving the farm and commercial grain storage markets and U.S. and international grain processing industries, providing important benefits to dealers and end customers and expanded opportunities for employees of both Butler and CTB."

John Holland, vice president of finance and chief financial officer of Butler, said: "In addition to share repurchases, with the cash received from this sale we will have the ability to make additional investments in the growth of our core non-residential construction businesses, where we have much greater critical mass and opportunities for sustainable competitive advantage."
Butler produces pre-engineered building systems and is a supplier of specialty components and construction services for the non-residential construction market.
